**Deconstructing YARN Integration**

I'm now detailing the architectural decisions and assumptions for YARN deployment and HDFS integration. My focus is on breaking down the implementation into specific tasks, covering HDFS staging, YARN orchestration, deployment property parsing, and asynchronous deployer refactoring, along with external library resolution.

**Estimating Detailed Task Effort**

technical_and_design_decisions: Leverage Spring Cloud Deployer (s-c-d) architecture and YARN REST APIs to handle application lifecycle and resource negotiation.
Implement HDFS file staging services to upload YARN application artifacts automatically before triggering deployment.
Refactor Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) ModuleLauncher to extend Spring Boot's standard JarLauncher API, removing duplicated custom classloading code.
Use standard Spring Cloud Deployer deployment properties format (e.g., module.*.yarn.app.name) to pass per-module queues, CPU, memory, and application metadata to YARN.
Implement asynchronous deployer operations using CompletableFuture and reactive task queues to avoid blocking CLI shell commands during cluster provisioning.
assumptions: Target environment has access to a working Hadoop HDFS and YARN ResourceManager cluster with REST endpoints enabled.
Java 17 runtime environment is available, compliant with Spring Framework 6.0 standards.
Build tools (Gradle/Maven) and standard repository structures are in place for module dependency resolution.
Development and testing will be performed on local Hadoop/YARN mini-clusters or dedicated test environments.

activities.activity_description: Define component interaction design for YARN deployer integration, HDFS automated deployment, and ModuleLauncher integration with Spring Boot's JarLauncher.
Implement automated uploading of YARN App packages into HDFS using manifests and integrate with xd-admin deployment orchestration.

activities.activity_name: YARN ResourceManager REST API & Module Grouping Support (U2)
activities.activity_description: Build REST integration with YARN ResourceManager to negotiate resource allocations and deploy application instances by groups (supporting CLOUDDATA and spring-cloud-data-yarn-app specifics).
Implement deployment property parsing for custom app names, YARN queue assignment, priority settings, and CPU/memory reservations per module.
Refactor deployer execution model to execute deployment commands asynchronously, enabling quick shell return and YARN task queuing.

activities.activity_name: ModuleLauncher Refactoring & External JAR Resolution (U5, U6, U8)
activities.activity_description: Refactor ModuleLauncher to extend Spring Boot's JarLauncher API and build uniform support for resolving and loading module-dependent external JAR libraries.
Develop unit tests, integration tests against YARN/HDFS endpoints, and verify end-to-end asynchronous deployment and external dependency resolution.
Document external library resolution patterns, Boot launcher integration mechanisms, and provide sample reference configurations for module developers.
